title: Failover overload: one server carries everything
question: Can Server A absorb all traffic after Server B is removed?
description: Each server can finish about 67 req/s (10 slots, 150 ms each). Together they handle 100 req/s comfortably. When Server B crashes for good at 20.5 s, Server A has to take everything.
assumptions: Abstract request-level model: no TCP, TLS, packets or real HTTP proxy semantics.
Each server has fixed concurrency slots and a FIFO queue; there is no CPU, memory or GC model.
Health probes bypass the request queue and answer instantly when the server is up.
Servers do not know when a client gave up; they finish the work and the late response is discarded.
No retries: every failed request is final.
Numbers are scenario inputs, not measured performance of any product.
expectedObservations: Server A's queue fills within a few seconds of the failover.
Latency rises to the service time plus the queue wait.
Once the queue is full, Server A rejects new requests even though it is healthy.
